p.x:
My aunt Nid is an artist. She lives in Chiang Mai and has a small gallery in the old city. She paints pictures of the mountains, rice fields and temples. Her paintings are bright and beautiful, and tourists love them.
When I visit her, she teaches me how to draw. "Start with simple shapes," she says. My drawings aren't very good, but she always tells me I have talent. She also designs traditional Thai patterns for clothes and bags, and she says Thai culture gives her lots of ideas.
Last year, a magazine took a photograph of her gallery and wrote a story about her. Now more people come to see her art. Aunt Nid says, "Being an artist is not easy, but I love my job. I'm lucky because I can do what I enjoy every day." One day, I want to be a writer and tell stories like the ones in her paintings.

"Hands of the North", a new exhibition at the Bangkok Art Centre, celebrates traditional crafts from northern Thailand. The collection includes more than 200 objects, from hand-woven silk and wooden sculptures to delicate pottery that is still made using methods hundreds of years old.
The most impressive part of the exhibition is a room of portraits. A young photographer spent two years visiting villages and photographing the craftspeople at work. Each portrait is displayed next to the object the person made, so visitors can see the face behind the art.
The exhibition also shows how these traditions inspire modern artists. One section displays creative designs by young Thai artists who combine old patterns with new materials. A famous novel about village life, written by a northern author in the 1950s, is quoted on the walls, adding a literary touch.
Overall, the show is a wonderful example of imagination and skill. My only criticism is that some labels are only in Thai, so foreign visitors may miss important information.

Few forms of art provoke as much debate as graffiti. To some, spray-painted words and images on public walls are simply vandalism that damages property and makes neighbourhoods look neglected. To others, graffiti is a powerful form of contemporary art, giving a voice to people who are excluded from traditional galleries.
The line between the two has become increasingly blurred. Some cities now commission artists to paint large murals on the sides of buildings, turning grey streets into tourist attractions. Works by the anonymous British artist Banksy, originally painted illegally, have been removed from walls and sold at auction for millions of pounds. Gallery curators who once ignored street art now organise major exhibitions of it.
Critics argue that much modern art, from graffiti to abstract painting, lacks the skill of older masterpieces. Supporters reply that art has always challenged aesthetic rules, and that the meaning of a work depends on how viewers interpret it. After all, many novels now considered great literature were attacked when they were first published.
Perhaps the real question is not whether graffiti is art, but who has the right to decide what art is.

q.th: หลัง a ต้องเป็นเอกพจน์

q.s: We [went] to the gallery [and] [see] [some] paintings.
q.fix: We went to the gallery and saw some paintings.

q.th: กริยาทั้งสองเป็นอดีต: saw

q.s: [Paint] is [my] [favourite] [hobby].
q.en: An activity as subject: Painting.
q.th: กิจกรรมเป็นประธาน: Painting

q.s: [Who] [did paint] [this] [picture]?

q.th: เมื่อ who เป็นประธาน ไม่ใช้ did: Who painted...?

q.fix: This novel was written by my favourite author in 1990.
q.en: With a past year and Past Simple passive, use 'in': in 1990.
q.th: ปีในอดีตกับ Past Simple ใช้ in: in 1990

q.en: If + past (imaginary) goes with 'would'.
q.th: If + อดีต (สมมติ) ใช้ would

q.fix: It is this painting, not the others, that has made her famous.

q.th: ประธานคือ this painting (เอกพจน์): has

q.fix: Painted in 1503, the Mona Lisa is considered by many people to be the greatest portrait ever.
q.en: The subject after the comma must be the thing that was painted, not 'many people'.
q.th: ประธานหลังจุลภาคต้องเป็นสิ่งที่ถูกวาด ไม่ใช่ many people
x: 'consider' is correct in the fixed sentence form.
